images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of Play2Evolve. (A) Player, Judge, and Designer agents use playtest feedback to guide code and video generation, turning runnable prototypes into playful games through defect repair, richer visual assets, and new gameplay. (B) GameCraft-Bench[29]scores and human ratings improve over initialization and Play2Code[22].

Figure 2:Overview of Play2Evolve’s recursive game development pipeline. (1) Initialization builds a runnable game with code and video generation. Playtest feedback guides Refinement to repair functional and visual defects, and Evolution to develop new gameplay and aesthetic improvements. (2) Each round turns agent play into diagnosis, planning, video and code revisions, candidate play, and A/B selection. (3) Behavior Skills guide later play, while adaptive generation selects static, single-subject, coupled-action, or full-scene materials.

Figure 3:Gameplay at V0, V1, and V2 for 3 games, with each pair showing the full frame (left) and an enlarged view of its yellow-boxed region (right). Game Refinement repairs visible defects, while Game Evolution enriches scene appearance and gameplay.
Figure 4:Successive evolution of two Godot games from V1 to V4. The highlighted regions show how each cycle adds player choices and visual feedback.

Figure 5:Three cases show how our agents use video generation to manage game assets and represent complex motion and object interactions. Panels (a), (b), and (c) show static-to-dynamic animation, coupled boxer-and-rope motion, and full-scene video integrated with game code.
Figure 6:Code-only and video-assisted gameplay in Neon Coast Rush and Lighthouse. Video materials enrich roadside scenery, road lighting, and the stormy sea in these examples.
